title: Choose the visual world for the Nova clinical portal
question: The roll assigned the Ward Label System. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Ward Label System
options.lineage: Thermal-printed specimen labels, ID wristbands and alert-stripe conventions on every ward
options.thesis: Every screening prints as a patient label: identity band on top, a risk flag stripe, and the result set like a lab value against its cut-off.
materials: real Code 128 barcodes of the patient ID
options.viewport: New screening: the photo and patient details on the left; on the right, a blank label that fills in as you type and prints its result stripe when analysis returns.
options.risk: Leaning too literal (fake paper textures, skeuomorphic curls) would read as a gimmick; it has to stay flat, crisp print grammar.

options.label: Bedside Instrument
options.lineage: Creator-hardware desk instrument: keycap grid, one orange commit key, amber status readout
options.thesis: The screening form as an instrument: one decisive Analyse key and a single-value readout of the jaundice likelihood.
options.case: Fuses partly: the one-key, one-readout discipline suits the bedside task, but gunmetal hardware reads as a gadget rather than hospital software.

options.label: Cutting-bench Rail
options.lineage: Film editor's select rail: perforated strip, punched frames, tape flags
options.thesis: Screenings strung along a rail as frames, flagged where you stopped, set-aside cases hung on pins below.
options.case: Fuses poorly: an orange-on-black editing bench fights a bright ward and drowns the red/amber/green risk code.

options.label: One-bit Desktop
options.lineage: Early black-and-white desktop: dither, windows, marching ants
options.thesis: Records as overlapping windows on one desktop plane.
options.case: Fuses poorly: dither-only greys cannot carry the colour-plus-label risk code the safety principle requires.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean hospital-software dashboard in the style of modern EHR and public-health service design, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Light sidebar navigation, a clear page title, results in well-spaced cards and tables.
canonCard.risk: Safe and familiar; easy to end up looking like every other admin template.
